# Bid prices for 3.5% Treasury Bond maturing Feb 1990
# Prices are in 32nds format

# From the Treasury Bulletins - March quotation for each year:
# Format is "whole.fraction" where fraction is in 32nds

prices = {

    1973: "73.30",  # 73 30/32
    1974: "70.16",  # 70 16/32
    1975: "76.22",  # 76 22/32
    1976: "82.04"   # 82 4/32  - actual March 1976
}

# Convert from 32nds to decimal
def price_to_decimal(price_str):
    whole, fraction = price_str.split('.')
    return int(whole) + int(fraction)/32

for year, price in prices.items():
    decimal_price = price_to_decimal(price)
    print(f"March {year}: {price} = {decimal_price:.4f}")

# Simple exponential smoothing with alpha = 0.3
alpha = 0.3

# Start with first observation
years = [1972, 1973, 1974, 1975, 1976]
observations = [price_to_decimal(prices[y]) for y in years]

print("\nObservations (USD):", observations)

# Calculate smoothed values
# S_1 = y_1
# S_t = alpha * y_{t-1} + (1-alpha) * S_{t-1} (for t > 1)
# Note: for one-step-ahead forecast, we use S_t to forecast y_{t+1}

smoothed = []
s = observations[0]  # S_1 = y_1

for i in range(1, len(observations)):
    # S_t = alpha * y_{t-1} + (1-alpha) * S_{t-1}
    s = alpha * observations[i-1] + (1 - alpha) * s
    smoothed.append(s)
    print(f"S_{years[i]} = {s:.4f} (forecast for {years[i]+1})")

print("\nSmoothed values:", smoothed)

# The one-step ahead forecast for March 1976 is S_1976 (the last smoothed value before the actual)
forecast_1976 = smoothed[-1]

print(f"Actual March 1976 price: {observations[-1]:.4f} USD")
print(f"Difference (actual - forecast): {observations[-1] - forecast_1976:.4f} USD")
